clue.text: Floors warp slowly at first with buff carpeting

parts.note: to warp is to bend or bow out of shape

indicators.note: carpeting covers something, so the word for buff is laid around the selected letter

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word slowly

parts.note: opening letter of slowly

explanation.surface: Someone describes timber floorboards slowly warping under a buff-coloured carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: Buff looks like a colour for the carpet, but it means an enthusiast; the carpet is wrapped round only part of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: To bowl someone over is to knock them flat or astonish them, the same as flooring them.

clue.text: Grasp Spooner's headlouse?

indicators.note: naming the Reverend Spooner means the opening sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: a head louse is a bug living in the hair

explanation.surface: A comic question about what Spooner would call a head louse.
explanation.walkthrough: HAIR BUG with its first sounds exchanged becomes BEAR HUG.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear hug is a tight, enveloping embrace, a kind of grasp around someone's body.

clue.text: You and I pretend to save time for team

parts.note: you and I together are we

indicators.note: saving something keeps it held safely inside, so the pretence wraps around the letter for time

parts.note: to sham is to pretend
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Two people agree to fake it to play for time on behalf of their side.
explanation.definitionFit: West Ham United is an English Premier League football club, so it is a team.

clue.text: Very difficult installing engine part in Yorkshire town

parts.note: so rough means very difficult or hard
carb is short for carburettor, a part of a petrol engine

explanation.surface: A tough job fitting a component to an engine in a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: SO ROUGH opens after its S to take CARB.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarborough is a seaside resort town on the North Yorkshire coast of England.

clue.text: Go low boarding vessel

indicators.note: boarding means getting on board, so one word goes inside the vessel

parts.note: a vase is a vessel for flowers
to low is what a cow does, to moo

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep your head down while getting onto a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Low is the verb for a cow's call, not the opposite of high.
explanation.definitionFit: Vamoose is slang for leaving hurriedly, an imperative meaning clear off or go away.

clue.text: One mistake at end of game in suburb of West London

indicators.note: at end of places the preceding pieces after the word for game

parts.note: RU is rugby union
I is the Roman numeral one
a slip is a small mistake

explanation.surface: Someone makes a single costly error at the finish of a match in a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: RU is the usual crossword shorthand for rugby union, the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruislip is a district in the London Borough of Hillingdon, on the western outskirts of the capital.

clue.text: Anchor, one swallowed by fish

indicators.note: something swallowed ends up inside the swallower, here the fish

parts.note: a bass is a fish
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.definitionFit: A basis is a foundation or mainstay, the thing that anchors or underpins something else.

clue.text: 'Cold-blooded' killer, swine wanting closure

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the word goes without its closing letter

parts.note: a boar is a male pig, a swine

explanation.surface: A heartless murderer, a real pig, is still waiting for the case to be closed.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes on Cold-blooded flag the literal sense: reptiles are cold-blooded.
explanation.definitionFit: A boa constrictor is a reptile that kills prey by squeezing, so literally a cold-blooded killer.

clue.text: Sixties singer bringing power into song in brief theatrical performance

indicators.note: in places the combined song piece within the shortened performance word
bringing power into the song puts that letter inside the tune's word
brief means cut short, so the performance word loses its final letter

parts.note: a show is a theatrical performance
an air is a song or tune
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A sixties star delivers a powerful number in a short stage turn.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here: power goes into the song first, and that whole unit then goes into the clipped performance word.
explanation.definitionFit: Helen Shapiro was a British pop singer whose hits, such as Walking Back to Happiness, came in the early 1960s.

clue.text: Top and bottom of small cube in trick

indicators.note: in a down clue the top and bottom of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: outermost letters of small
eight is two cubed, a cube number

explanation.surface: A sleight of hand with a little die, shown on its top and bottom faces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight means deceptive dexterity, as in sleight of hand, so it is a trick or cunning ruse.

clue.text: Lost when navigating?

parts.note: surface reading: a navigator who has lost their way
setter's reading: a phrase meaning both bewildered and out on the ocean sailing

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means confused, and also literally out on the ocean, where navigating happens.
explanation.definitionFit: At sea is an idiom for bewildered or perplexed, while also describing a ship out on the ocean.

clue.text: Affluent London district with bitter constituents, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the words are judged on how they are heard, not spelt

parts.note: bitter is a kind of beer, and its constituents are what it is made of

explanation.surface: A wealthy part of London reputedly made up of resentful residents.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British style of beer, so it is made of ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Maida Vale is a wealthy residential area of north-west London near St John's Wood.

clue.text: Quiet when kids finally kicked out, eh?

indicators.note: kicked out means removed, so that letter is thrown out of the word for quiet

parts.note: hush means quiet

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of kids

parts.note: final letter of kids

explanation.surface: A parent remarks that the house goes quiet once the children are finally thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Huh and eh are both interjections expressing puzzlement or asking for something to be repeated.

clue.text: Blandishments from Wellington at Waterloo?

parts.note: a wellington is a rubber boot
a licking is a heavy defeat, as Napoleon suffered at Waterloo

explanation.surface: A history question about what the Duke of Wellington dished out at Waterloo.
explanation.walkthrough: Wellington is the boot, not the duke; the licking is the defeat he gave Napoleon.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootlicking is servile flattery used to win favour, which is what blandishments are.

clue.text: Tip over beer in London station

indicators.note: in a down entry over means placed above, so the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: to cock is to tip or tilt, as with a hat
Foster's is a brand of Australian lager

explanation.surface: Someone knocks over a pint in a London tube station.
explanation.walkthrough: Tip over reads as knock over, but over is just the order for this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockfosters is the northern terminus of the Piccadilly line on the London Underground.

clue.text: Stick figure, head in Hangman to go — in trouble up there?

parts.note: to gum is to stick

indicators.note: to go says that letter must leave the word for figure

parts.note: three is a figure, a number

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, the one to be taken

parts.note: leading letter of Hangman

explanation.surface: A stick figure in a game of hangman loses its head and is in a dire spot.
explanation.walkthrough: To be up a gum tree is a British idiom for being in serious difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase up a gum tree means in trouble, so the gum tree is where trouble is, up there.

clue.text: Recognise extract

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to identify or discern something among others
second meaning: to remove or pull something out

explanation.definitionFit: To pick out is to identify someone in a crowd, and also to select and remove an item.

clue.text: Great Arsenal leader in Italian stallion perhaps tackled by those from Chelsea?

indicators.note: being tackled means being grabbed and held, so the Chelsea items surround the rest

parts.note: Chelsea buns are sticky currant buns

indicators.note: leader asks for the opening letter of Italian

parts.note: first letter of Italian
a gee-gee is a child's word for a horse, such as a stallion

explanation.surface: A football tale: Arsenal's star, an Italian powerhouse, is brought down by Chelsea defenders.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal looks like the football club but means weaponry; Chelsea gives buns, not players.
explanation.definitionFit: Big guns are heavy artillery, a formidable store of weapons, so a great arsenal.

clue.text: Bananas, except top banana

parts.note: bar means except, as in all bar one
the top banana is the boss, the king

explanation.surface: A greengrocer insists every banana is mad apart from the very best one.
explanation.walkthrough: Bananas and banana suggest fruit, but bananas means crazy and top banana means leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Barking, short for barking mad, is British slang for crazy, which bananas also means.

clue.text: Catch monkeys in valley when ground cleared

indicators.note: in places the monkeys inside the shortened valley word
in a down entry the ground is the bottom, so clearing it removes the final letter

parts.note: a glen is a Scottish valley
monkeys as a name for mischievous children, imps

explanation.surface: Trying to trap monkeys in a valley once the land has been cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the ground is the bottom letter, so the valley loses its last letter before the monkeys go in. Monkeys and imps are both playful mischief-makers.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch a glimpse is to see something briefly, so catch as a noun or verb of brief sight fits.

clue.text: Food processor plugged in connects to machine

indicators.note: plugged in says the answer is lodged inside the following words

parts.note: letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: Instructions for a kitchen gadget that only works once it is plugged in and linked up.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen appliance reading is a decoy; the processor of food is a body organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The stomach digests and breaks down what we eat, so it processes food inside the body.

clue.text: Stole 23 across?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a scarf worn round the neck
second meaning: something that silences, the answer to 23 across being a gag

explanation.walkthrough: Stole looks like the past tense of steal, but it is a scarf. The answer to 23 across is GAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A muffler is a warm scarf, and also anything that deadens sound, as a gag stifles speech.

clue.text: Art is with me modelling for great artistes

indicators.note: modelling means shaping as clay is shaped, so the letters are reformed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A self-important artist claims that their posing is itself art.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestri is the Italian plural of maestro, a title for distinguished musicians and artists.

clue.text: Swine loses top match

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is lost

parts.note: a blighter is a contemptible person, a swine

explanation.surface: A bad sport loses the deciding game of a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: Blighter is mild British slang for an annoying or contemptible person.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a device for producing a flame, doing the job of a match.

clue.text: Maiden coming into Bank via Victoria, say?

indicators.note: coming into means entering, so the maiden goes inside the word for bank

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
a gal is a girl, a maiden

explanation.surface: A woman travels into Bank station by way of Victoria on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: Bank and Victoria look like tube stations; Victoria is the queen, so via a queen means in royal fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Regally means in a royal manner, as a queen such as Victoria would act.

clue.text: A tight shirt features again on back of striker in Scottish team

indicators.note: the jumbled shirt features, or includes, the word for again within it

parts.note: last letter of striker
taken as written
the letters of shirt rearranged

indicators.note: tight means drunk, and a drunken shirt is jumbled up

parts.note: over means again, as in do it over

explanation.surface: A footballer's figure-hugging shirt shows up once more on the striker's back.
explanation.walkthrough: Tight looks like a description of the shirt but is the anagram signal, meaning drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Raith Rovers is a professional football club based in Kirkcaldy, Fife, in Scotland.

clue.text: Quiet quip

explanation.definitionFit: To gag someone is to silence or quieten them, and a gag is also a joke or witty remark.

taken as written
to tan someone's hide is to whip them

explanation.walkthrough: Whip looks like the parliamentary post next to politician, but it means to beat, TAN.

clue.text: Career issue

explanation.walkthrough: Career here is a verb, to rush along, not a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To run is to career along quickly, and a run is a batch of copies printed, an issue.

taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, to raise or lift someone up in esteem.

clue.text: Where one might be putting London park

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the area of a golf course around the hole
second meaning: a royal park beside Buckingham Palace

explanation.walkthrough: Putting is the golf stroke, not placing. Green Park is a royal park in central London.

clue.text: Bath full of beer ultimately quaffed by difficult setter

parts.note: hairy is slang for difficult or dangerous
